questions.answer: Social events to meet people. Friends are important when your´e in a foreign country.

questions.answer: Go travelling. Its nice to explore. And its also a good way to get friends. Also study.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Of course there were some differences, but i felt like the teachers were very tolerant towards Erasmus-students, which was great.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Its difficult. It was easy to socialize with other international students. But with the locals, you have to do something active. It doesn´t just happen by itself.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: To some extent everything seemed to be more loosely organized than in Copenhagen. The Leistungspunkte-System was very different than in Denmark, and i often felt like i would get more ECTS-points for an assignment/test in Danmark. It was hard to make it all add up, where in Copenhagen you would just write to assignments in the end of the year and get 30 ects-points.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The beauty. Heidelberg, and some of the other smaller cities (Weinheim, Ladenburg) were so pretty.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Dont forget to enjoy it. It will soon be over.
2. Try to get a good relationship with you professors. That can help a lot in the end. 
3. Try to challenge yourself academically. Dont be afraid of failing, taking a hard course.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Dont drink too much. Its not nice if you spend too many days having hangover, especially when youre there for such a short time. 

Erasmus doesnt feel stressfull in the beginning. But in the end, when exams arrive, it suddenly goes from 0-100. Be prepared. If you can already begin to write parts of you assignments in the semester period, it might be easier for you.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Travelling with friends. Going to northern Germany, France and Italy in a van. I even went to Malmø, Sweden: a city ive never been to, even know i live in Copenhagen.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer:
The exams. The assignments which i had to write in the end, in a foreign language, which very little time. 
The Bureaucracy. A lot of things you figure out
